title: Suitability of Externally Masked FX Constructions
summary: Generic tradeoffs weaken externally masked FX designs, while key-schedule integration improves resistance; whether FX remains suitable for new block ciphers is unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the FX-construction remains an appropriate basis for new block-cipher designs when its masking keys are external to the core cipher's key schedule, given that generic time-memory-data tradeoffs can reduce the effective key size and enable online key-recovery attacks on designs such as PRINCE and PRIDE with semi-practical complexities. The unresolved task is to establish whether these vulnerabilities make externally masked FX-constructions unsuitable for new designs, or whether integrating the masking keys into the core cipher's key schedules provides a generally adequate security improvement with little overhead against such generic attacks.

scope.domain: Block-cipher design and generic cryptanalysis of FX-constructions with external or key-schedule-integrated masking keys.
parameters: Masking-key placement: external to or integrated into the core cipher's key schedule
Time, memory, and data: attack resources involved in the generic tradeoffs
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether generic vulnerabilities rule out externally masked FX-constructions for new designs, or whether integrating masking keys into core key schedules is a generally adequate low-overhead defense.

citations.label: Cryptanalytic Time-Memory-Data Tradeoffs for FX-Constructions with Applications to PRINCE and PRIDE

progress.summary: The paper presents generic time-memory-data tradeoffs that reduce effective key size and enable semi-practical online key recovery against PRINCE and PRIDE. It then gives a key-schedule integration tweak and uses these findings to question FX in new designs.
citation_labels: Itai Dinur et al., Cryptanalytic Time-Memory-Data Tradeoffs for FX-Constructions with Applications to PRINCE and PRIDE
